query: how to give an ai agent access to your apps safely
title: Give an AI agent access to your apps safely | 50agents
description: Give an AI agent only the apps its job needs, read access by default, and an approval on every send, payment or permission change. A checklist.
h1: How to give an AI agent access to your apps safely
answer: Connect only the apps one job needs, let the AI agent read alone, and make every send, payment or permission change wait for your approval.
Keep a log of its actions and know how to cut access fast.

body.p: OWASP calls it "Excessive Agency": the AI agent has more functions, more permissions or more freedom to act than its job needs.

The classic case: an assistant that summarises your email can also send email. Someone mails you hidden instructions, it reads them, and forwards your private mail. Nothing was hacked. It used a permission it never needed.
Text an AI agent reads can carry instructions. You cannot stop it reading, so limit what it can do after.

ul: Does the AI agent use my login, or a connection I can limit?
Which actions can it take without me, and can I change that per AI agent?
Is the approval enforced by the product, or written in the prompt?
Where is the log of what it did?
When I disconnect an app, what stops working?

steps.title: One job, its own apps
steps.body: Connect the apps this job needs and nothing else. An AI agent that drafts replies needs your inbox, not your accounting app.

steps.title: Read by default
steps.body: Reading is low risk; changing is not. Start every AI agent read-only and add write actions one by one, when a job needs them.

steps.title: Narrow scopes on the consent screen
steps.body: Grant the smallest set of permissions the feature needs. If a tool asks for full access to everything on day one, ask why.

steps.title: Approvals the tool enforces
steps.body: "Ask before sending" in the instructions guides the AI but cannot stop it. The approval must be a step the software will not skip.

note.text: A line in the prompt is a wish, not a lock. Check the send really waits for your tap.

steps.title: Sort actions by what they can break
steps.body: Sends to customers, payments, deleting, sharing and adding people are high risk. Label changes and notes in your own tools are low. Ask: does it write, can it be undone, does money move?

steps.title: Keep a log of every action
steps.body: What it did, in which app, and why. You will need it the first time a customer asks "why did I get this email?".

steps.title: Know how to cut it off
steps.body: Pause the AI agent, and know where to revoke its connection: in the tool, and in the app's own security settings (Google Account, Microsoft, HubSpot).

captain.line: In 50agents an AI agent uses only the apps in its plan, reads on its own, and asks in Needs you before any change. Every action lands in Activity.

wrong.title: Prompt injection through email or web pages
wrong.body: A message tells the AI agent to do something. If it can only read and draft, the worst case is a bad draft you decline.

wrong.title: It inherited all your access
wrong.body: You connected your admin account to an AI agent that needed one mailbox. Use a narrower account or a shared mailbox where you can.

wrong.title: Approval fatigue
wrong.body: Fifty approvals a day and you start tapping yes without reading. Cut what asks to what matters, and batch the rest into one report.

wrong.title: A stale connection keeps working
wrong.body: Someone left, or a project ended, and the AI agent still has their access. Review connections monthly and remove what no AI agent uses.

wrong.title: Customer data in the wrong place
wrong.body: An AI agent copies contact details into a shared channel or open sheet. Say in its instructions where data may go, and check its first runs.

faqs.q: Should an AI agent use my login or its own account?
faqs.a: Its own, limited one where the app allows it, such as a shared mailbox or a restricted user. Where it must use yours, limit what it may do without asking.

faqs.q: Are OAuth permissions enough on their own?
faqs.a: No. They decide what the AI agent can reach, not what it should do. Pair them with approvals on risky actions and a log.

faqs.q: How do I take access away?
faqs.a: Pause or delete the AI agent, disconnect the app in the tool, and revoke the app in the provider's security settings, such as your Google Account's third-party access page.
